answers.answer: Put each Player ID upright in its plastic stand visibly in front of the player. Give each player the Voting set matching their color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not playing and keep their own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: ID card upright in its plastic stand; remove cards targeting colors that are not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down and keep values hidden.

answers.answer: There is no individual turn order; voting is simultaneous. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. After everyone has chosen, reveal all choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: no individual turn order. Vote: you may change your chosen card until cards are revealed; reveal all choices simultaneously.

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is required. The player with the most votes is the Target, so with totals of three, two, and two, Red alone is the Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.” The example says four and three are different totals, and Blue alone is Target.

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. Without successful Ambush protection, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to other elimination and Ambush rules.
answers.evidence: Vote: if several players tie for the most votes, all are Targets; with tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.

answers.answer: Ambush does not count as a vote, so Red has zero counted votes; Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow give Red and Yellow one vote each. They tie as Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red may eliminate one player who voted for Red, which here is Yellow. Yellow is eliminated, while Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow; Red also survives through Ambush. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: Three-player example: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes Red, Pink votes Yellow; Red and Yellow tie and are Targets; Yellow is eliminated, Red survives, and Pink survives after voting for tied Target Yellow.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the Target choose one of the players who voted for them to eliminate. They may not eliminate all four, and may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: chooses one of the players who voted for them; cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.

answers.answer: The Ambush fails, and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors after the vote and Ambush effects, continue with another Conspire and Vote among the surviving players only.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: three or more survivors continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. Components: each bar is one card valued at 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card, places it face down, and, when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes Share, Steal, Grab One & Go; may discuss; each chooses one face down; reveal simultaneously when both are ready.

answers.answer: With no survivors, each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, even if eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars. Leave those four bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: none survive—players not participating in the final vote each receive one deck bar; leave the four central bars and add no new bars. Special Rules clarifies final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Share gives each player 2.

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Share receives zero central bars, and the finalist choosing Steal receives all four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Steal gives Share 0 and Steal 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar, and the Steal finalist receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table and note: Grab One & Go against Steal gives Grab One & Go 1 and the opponent 3.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar, and the Share finalist receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table and note: Grab One & Go against Share gives Grab One & Go 1 and the opponent 3.

answers.answer: Each takes one central bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, deal two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: both Grab One & Go—each receives one, leave two central, and add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: both Steal—neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of a round after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: check at end of round after bars are awarded; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; highest point total wins.

answers.answer: The tied qualifying leaders conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in that round: stand all IDs upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: repeat Showdowns until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Turn Structure: if there is no winner, everyone returns and all IDs are stood upright for another round.

answers.answer: Before every vote, conspiracy lasts roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication is allowed, openly or secretly, including texting or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: roughly a minute and a half at most; any communication method, openly or secretly, including texting and showing a Voting card; the game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the visible ID color of the player you target and place it face down in front of yourself. If you suspect you are the Target and want to defend yourself, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; target with the card matching that player's visible ID color; use your Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: Vote: knock down eliminated players' IDs and leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.

answers.answer: Because all four central bars were awarded, none remain to carry over. If nobody wins, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down to make the next central pool of four, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: if the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars; central pool is refilled to four as needed.

answers.answer: No. Blue remains the sole Target because Blue's four votes are more than Purple's three; Blue's successful Ambush protects Blue but does not change the tally or promote Purple to Target. Voters for Purple do not survive on that basis: they are eliminated for failing to vote for Blue.
answers.evidence: Larger example: Blue alone is Target—four and three differ; Ambush does not promote runner-up; players who voted Purple are eliminated for not voting Blue.

answers.answer: The booklet's tie instruction is to have tied leaders conduct a Final Showdown, repeating as needed until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. However, it does not specify how to arrange a Showdown among three or more tied players; that procedure is unsupported and requires publisher clarification.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as needed; the unresolved source limitation says card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players and give no arrangement for three or more tied leaders.

answers.answer: Yes. In an extra two-player Showdown where both Steal, each player outside that pair receives one Gold Bar from the deck. The totals of all players at the table are compared afterward, so an outside player receiving that bar could become the single highest-scoring winner.
answers.evidence: Scoring: use the same deck rewards in extra Showdowns, compare all players afterward, and an outside player can become the single highest-scoring winner.
